title: The Self-Improvement Problem
abstract: arXiv:2610.21646v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: With the rise of large language models, agentic systems are becoming increasingly autonomous, as they write code, call tools, revise prompts, and propose modifications to their own components. This autonomy raises a fundamental question for safe self-improvement: can an automated gate like a reward model or an automated reviewer reliably decide whether a proposed update should be accepted? The difficulty is structural. The gate must be a terminating, computable procedure, while the property we ultimately care about, namely whether an update is a genuine semantic improvement, depends on potentially unbounded program behavior. We formalize this mismatch by modeling agents as programs and defining improvement in terms of a semantic score that need not be computable. We study two evaluation abstractions. translated_abstract: 随着大语言模型的兴起，智能体系统正变得日益自主：它们编写代码、调用工具、修改提示词，并提议对自身组件进行修改。这种自主性引发了一个关于安全自我改进的根本性问题：像奖励模型或自动化审阅者这样的自动化门控机制，能否可靠地判定一个提议的更新是否应当被接受？这一困难是结构性的。门控机制必须是一个可终止、可计算的过程，而我们最终真正关心的属性——即某个更新是否构成真正的语义改进——却可能依赖于无界的程序行为。我们通过将智能体建模为程序，并以一个未必可计算的语义评分来定义“改进”，从而形式化了这种不匹配。我们研究了两种评估抽象：第一种是批准或拒绝某个更新的认证器；第二种是搜索过程，它在给定一个提案生成器……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文将智能体的自我改进形式化为可计算性问题，指出奖励模型等自动化门控机制虽必须是可终止、可计算的过程，却无法可靠判定一个更新是否构成真正的语义改进，从而揭示了自我改进的结构性内在限制。
en_tdlr: This paper formalizes the self-improvement problem by modeling agents as programs, showing that automated gates such as reward models—being terminating, computable procedures—cannot reliably certify whether an update constitutes a genuine semantic improvement.
